teaser: How an sgit vault acts like a database on a server that cannot read: one key-derived mutable file, everything else immutable.
core_idea: Everything in a vault is encrypted on the client so a fully compromised server leaks nothing confidential. To act like a database anyway, a client computes the name of the one mutable file, the ref, from the read key with an HMAC; decrypting it gives the head commit, then the tree, then the file, in about four plain requests. Every other object is named by the hash of its ciphertext, so it can be verified without a key and cached for ever, and refreshing a site means re-reading one file. On the web, vaults are read file by file or run as apps in a sandboxed frame with a narrow sg bridge, where behaviour policies come next.
